newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says Clinton turns out to be the sick one.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Clinton turns out to be the sick one.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin, relishing his return to health, said on Monday he had foiled predictions that he would be the sick man at this week's Russia-U.S. summit in Helsinki.
"You see no one is insured against illness. Bill Clinton suddenly also got ill," the Russian president said in interview, extracts of which were aired on Russian Television.
Yeltsin, 66, has appeared reinvigorated recently after almost eight months of illness -- first heart problems and then pneumonia.
The 50-year-old American leader, meanwhile, had to undergo surgery last Friday after he slipped and twisted his knee.
Yeltsin and Clinton agreed to put off their planned March 19 summit in Helsinki for a day to allow Clinton more time to recover.
"They said that a sick Yeltsin and a healthy Clinton would come to Helsinki and it turns out the other way around," Yeltsin said.
The Kremlin leader, who had quintuple heart bypass surgery in November, came under fierce attack last year from critics who said he was unable to rule Russia and should step down.
He reaffirmed his grip on power on Monday.
"I am in good form today. Today I am able, so to say, to rule the state and in fact in better form today than before the illness and I will of course rule Russia up to new elections in 2000."
